title: Text, background, and border colours
learningObjectives: Explain text, background, and border colours and apply it correctly in a small CSS example.

understand.concept: The color property sets an element's text colour and often supplies the inherited currentColor value. background-color paints the element's background area. border-color sets the colour of its border, provided a visible border style and width are present.
understand.whyItMatters: These properties affect different visual parts of the box. A background may extend behind padding, while the border is drawn around the padding and content. Text colour does not automatically guarantee sufficient contrast.
understand.analogy: Think of a labelled card: ink colour, paper colour, and frame colour are separate choices. A readable design checks the relationship between the ink and the surface.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy helps build intuition, but the browser follows the CSS specifications and computed-style rules rather than human intentions.

explain.narrative: The card uses a dark text colour, pale background, and distinct border. Change each property separately to see which region it affects.

questions.prompt: What is the best way to learn the effect of a CSS value?

Add unrelated declarations until it looks right
Assume every browser calculates styles identically in every context
